title: A private network with controlled egress
summary: 40 high schools in Jalisco publish grades on a portal. The state Education Ministry requires that neither the servers nor the database can be reached from the internet.

requirements.1: {{s1}} lets the private servers download patches from the internet, but nobody outside can open a connection to them.
requirements.2: All outbound web traffic goes through {{s2}}, an intermediary that only lets it reach the domains of the SAT, the bank and the patch repository.
requirements.3: {{s3}} makes only the app servers talk to the database on port 3306, whatever subnet they are in, and lets the reply come back on its own.
requirements.4: {{s4}} gives administrators a terminal on servers with no public IP, without opening port 22 to the internet, and keeps a record of every session.
requirements.5: {{s5}} takes the PDF report cards from the servers to object storage without going out to the internet or through slot 1.
requirements.6: {{s6}} keeps the source, destination and port of the servers' network traffic to investigate a scan.
requirements.7: The grades database listens on port 3306 and lives in a private subnet, with no public IP.

s1.explanation: A NAT gateway gives resources without public IPs internet access without exposing them to incoming internet connections.
s1.hint_cue: nobody outside can open a connection to them

s2.explanation: OCI Network Firewall filters by URL and FQDN: it can restrict egress traffic to a list of domains, such as the SAT, bank and patch domains.
s2.hint_cue: only lets it reach the domains

s3.explanation: An NSG applies only to the VNICs you choose and its rule can use another NSG as the source, so 3306 opens to the app servers whatever their subnet; with stateful rules, the reply passes on its own.

s4.explanation: OCI Bastion gives restricted, time-limited access over SSH sessions to resources with no public endpoint, and Audit records every call to the Bastion API, such as the one that creates a session.
s4.hint_cue: without opening port 22 to the internet

s5.explanation: The service gateway lets the VCN reach Oracle services such as Object Storage privately, with no internet gateway or NAT gateway; traffic stays on the Oracle network fabric and never crosses the internet.
s5.hint_cue: without going out to the internet or through slot 1

s6.explanation: VCN flow logs record details about traffic that was accepted or rejected by security list or NSG rules.

oci-internet-gateway.s1: With an internet gateway, instances in a public subnet start connections to the internet and also receive inbound connections from the internet.

oci-security-list.s2: A security list applies IP, protocol and port rules to every VNIC in a subnet; it does not filter by domain name.
oci-security-list.s3: A security list applies its rules to every VNIC in the whole subnet; Oracle recommends NSGs to separate application security from the subnet layout.

oci-site-to-site-vpn.s4: Site-to-Site VPN is an IPSec connection between the on-premises network and the VCN; it is not the restricted, time-limited SSH sessions that Bastion provides, whose creation is recorded in Audit.

oci-lpg.s5: A local peering gateway connects two VCNs in the same region so their resources can communicate over private IPs; private access to Object Storage comes from the service gateway. Oracle recommends routing between VCNs through an upgraded DRG.

oci-audit.s6: Audit records calls to public APIs, such as Bastion's; it does not keep the network traffic between VNICs.
